To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) nonaxisymmetric equilibria exist in isopedically magnetizied singular isothermal disks at all dimensionless rotation rates, including zero, and (ii) such equilibria terminate at a critical dimensionless rotation rate that is independent of magnetic field strength.

(1) the equilibrium configuration of a magnetized singular isothermal disk (M=1), without the assumption of axisymmetry, is a lopsided (lops) configuration with a single, broad, elongated, and nonaxisymmetric density enhancement; and (2) lops sequences bifurcate from the underlying axisymmetric sequence (M=0) of singular isothermal disks at any dimensionless rate of rotation (omega) but always terminate in shock waves before they have a realistic chance
the formation of multiple stars from singular isothermal disks requires the loss of magnetic flux and that this loss of magnetic flux can be achieved by a rapid (i.e, dynamical) collapse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of magnetic fields in star formation and with the role of star formation in galactic evolution.
the role of magnetic fields in the formation of multiple stellar systems.
the role of magnetic fields in the formation of multiple stars, and with the possible existence of a new class of astrophysical magnetic flux tubes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of multiple stars from smooth, magnetized, singular isothermal disk precursors requires a mechanism for rapid flux loss.
the formation of multiple stars is a complex process that depends critically on the details of the initial conditions.
the formation of binary stars is possible from a singular isothermal disk, provided it is initially supercritical and is allowed to lose magnetic flux rapidly enough to become subcritical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the class of singular isothermal disks we consider here, the only stable, dynamically relaxed equilibrium configuration is the axisymmetric one.
the inclusion of magnetic fields in the theory of star formation is a necessary step toward the understanding of binary and multiple star formation.
the formation of binary stars from smooth, magnetized disks is a problem that has not yet been solved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inclusion of magnetic fields in the context of self-gravitating, rotating systems can have profound implications for their stability.
the formation of binaries and multiples from smooth starting states is not a generic consequence of the self-gravitating, isothermal nature of the collapse.
the formation of binary stars and multiple systems from smooth starting states requires that the collapse be supercritical and that the magnetic flux be dynamically lost.
